cards.title: "Kiske liye hai?" isn't gossip
cards.body: It's one of the most useful questions asked at the counter. Here's why your chemist asks it every time.

cards.title: Age changes the dose
cards.body: Children and older adults often need different doses or forms. The same medicine isn't right for everyone.

cards.title: Other medicines matter
cards.body: If it's for Papa, who already takes BP and sugar medicines, the chemist may want to check for clashes.

cards.title: Some conditions need extra care
cards.body: Pregnancy, kidney problems or allergies can change what's suitable. Knowing who it's for helps them ask the right follow-up.

cards.title: Right form for the person
cards.body: Syrup for a small child, something easier to swallow for Nani. The answer shapes what's handed over.

cards.title: Answer fully, not "ghar ke liye"
cards.body: Give the age, who it's for, and anything relevant. It takes seconds and makes the medicine safer.

takeaway: Your chemist asks who the medicine is for because age, conditions and other medicines all affect what's safe.
share: Send this to the person who says "bas de do bhaiya" at the counter.
